summary: An iterator hands out values one at a time with next(). A generator function, written function*, uses yield to build an iterator in a few lines and makes each value only when it is asked for.
notes: next() returns an object like { value: 3, done: false }. When nothing is left, it returns { value: undefined, done: true }.
A class becomes usable in for...of and [...x] by defining a [Symbol.iterator]() method that returns an object with next().
take(4).toArray() stops the endless generator after 4 values. take() is an iterator helper added in Node 22.
pitfall: A generator can only be looped over once. A second for...of loop over the same generator object runs zero times with no error.
contrast: JavaScript has yield like Python, but the function needs a * and next() returns { value, done } objects. A used-up iterator returns done: true instead of raising StopIteration (Python) or throwing NoSuchElementException (Java).
